01

01 / GTM SYSTEMS + REVENUE ENABLEMENT

Turning analyst influence into a measurable enterprise growth engine

Six Five Media - The Futurum Group | 2024-present

Challenge

Six Five had strong analyst credibility and a high-volume content engine, but its content, demand generation, and revenue operations needed to function as one measurable GTM system. The website also needed to evolve from a host- and show-led presence into a discoverable media portfolio with clearer audience and partner journeys.

What I led

  • Restructured content and GTM operations around repeatable media products, priority audiences, industry moments, and revenue motions rather than one-off publishing.
  • Built ICP account and lead lists in ZoomInfo, activated segmented nurture sequences in HubSpot, and connected engagement signals and handoffs to Salesforce opportunities and influenced-revenue reporting.
  • Led the website transformation into a structured media platform with distinct content, podcast, summit, event, host, and partner pathways; aligned social distribution to grow audience and drive qualified traffic back to owned experiences.
  • Created an audience funnel from monthly viewers to subscribers to regular viewers, then used retention, CPA, and format performance to guide investment.
  • Established ABM tiers, funnel definitions, campaign calendars, enablement assets, outbound sequences, competitive proof, and performance reporting with Sales and RevOps.
  • Improved search and answer-engine readiness through topic-led content organization, indexable content hubs, expert/host attribution, clearer page intent, and answer-oriented pathways across editorial and commercial content.

Evidence

  • Inbound increased 6x after the new website launched, then grew another 50% the following year.
  • Marketing programs influenced $1M in revenue.
  • Contributed to approximately 25% YoY client revenue growth.
  • Grew YouTube from roughly 45,000 to more than 138,000 subscribers.
  • Improved paid subscriber CPA from $0.56 in 2025 to $0.32 YTD 2026.
  • Generated 47.49M X impressions, 16.82M LinkedIn impressions, and 7.85M YouTube views over the latest 12-month period.

Selected artifacts

Six Five Media 2026 Marketing Strategy & Growth Plan · ZoomInfo -> HubSpot -> Salesforce revenue workflow · Website and content architecture before/after review · Competitive battlecard: Six Five Media vs. TechTarget · Corporate-event and branded-series case studies · Audience information, partner decks, and outbound sequences

Internal GTM system

ZoomInfo ICP lists -> HubSpot nurture and engagement -> Salesforce opportunity handoff -> influenced-revenue reporting.

Consumer growth engine

Searchable content hubs + events, summit, podcast, host, and partner journeys -> owned audience growth -> qualified inbound.

AEO + search visibility

Topic architecture, explicit page intent, expert attribution, indexable content, and answer-led formats designed to improve discovery in search and AI answers.

02

02 / ADOPTION + RETENTION

Connecting product behavior to conversion, retention, and lifetime value

ConsumerDirect / SmartCredit | 2022-2024

Challenge

Retention analysis needed to move beyond correlation and identify the product behaviors most likely to move trial users onto the recurring-revenue “money line” and keep paying customers engaged.

What I led

  • Partnered with data teams to evaluate feature usage against first-bill conversion and monthly renewal probability.
  • Identified ID Fraud Insurance and Live Alerts activation as high-value trial behaviors; modeled the incremental revenue impact of increased adoption.
  • Identified recurring 1B report updates and customer actions as retention signals, then translated findings into lifecycle and in-product opportunities.
  • Built segmented email, SMS, push, and in-app programs across acquisition, activation, engagement, renewal, reactivation, and monetization.

Evidence

  • Reduced churn 60% in six months, preserving $1.8M in annualized revenue.
  • Generated $10.5M in customer lifetime value and improved average retention from 3-4 months to 5 months.
  • Scaled a new application from zero to 25,000+ users in six months and added 70,000+ active users to an existing subscription product.
  • Modeled $930,852 in annual value for each combined 10-point lift in key trial activation and monthly report-refresh behaviors.

Selected artifacts

Feature Adoption & Retention Executive Summary · Customer journey and lifecycle maps · SmartCredit value proposition and proof-point messaging · Lifecycle and transactional campaign examples

03 / PRODUCT ADOPTION + EXPERIMENTATION

Designing a measurable rollout for a new in-app engagement channel

ConsumerDirect / Hogo

Challenge

Important education, privacy, rewards, and referral experiences were difficult to discover. Only about 8% of users had visited privacy tips, and tips views represented less than 0.7% of app opens over the measured 60-day period.

What I led

  • Developed the business case and rollout strategy for Braze Content Cards as a personalized, persistent in-app surface.
  • Mapped use cases across onboarding, feature discovery, education, upsell, referrals, feedback, loyalty, and retention.
  • Defined audience criteria, message concepts, UI placements, implementation dependencies, and testing opportunities.
  • Connected the proposal to a standardized campaign process covering objectives, journey mapping, test methodology, compliance, QA, launch, measurement, and cross-functional readout.

Evidence

  • Created a decision-ready proposal balancing a $6,000 platform cost against multiple adoption and monetization use cases.
  • Established a reusable campaign framework spanning Marketing, Product, Design, Data, Operations, Sales/Accounting, and Compliance.
  • Defined a funnel measurement pattern from sends to clicks, landing-page behavior, signup, and enhanced reactivation.

04 / TECHNICAL POSITIONING + LAUNCHES

Relaunching acquired photonic technology and bringing complex engineering releases to market

Synopsys | 2018-2021

Challenge

Following the acquisition of PhoeniX B.V., Synopsys needed to integrate OptoDesigner into a broader electronic-photonic design automation story while continuing to launch specialized optical products such as LucidShape. The portfolio had to be understandable to expert engineers, enterprise buyers, foundry partners, and industrial markets.

What I led

  • Supported 4-6 major releases per year with product, engineering, sales, and data teams.
  • Helped relaunch the acquired PhoeniX Software portfolio as Synopsys Photonic Solutions, translating OptoDesigner from a standalone PIC-layout product into part of a connected Synopsys EDA workflow.
  • Built technical messaging for the flow from OptSim photonic circuit simulation to OptoDesigner layout and verification, and later OptoCompiler schematic-driven electronic-photonic co-design with PrimeSim SPICE / HSPICE.
  • Connected platform capabilities to industrial use cases including 5G communications, cloud and data-center interconnects, high-speed optical communications, sensing, and semiconductor design.
  • Led product-feature and version-update marketing for the LucidShape automotive lighting portfolio, including design, simulation, visualization, light-guide, freeform-optics, pixel-light, CATIA, and manufacturability enhancements.
  • Developed positioning, product pages, solution content, learning resources, launch releases, case studies, fact sheets, and technical enablement materials.
  • Built partner and academic motions involving photonic foundries and university programs; supported messaging for automotive, LiDAR, AR/VR, biomedical, and semiconductor use cases.

Evidence

  • Helped turn the PhoeniX photonics portfolio from approximately -$5M net to profitability within two years.
  • Established a unified portfolio narrative connecting photonic device, circuit, layout, verification, and electronic co-design workflows.
  • A Photonics West program generated 150+ booth visitors and approximately 10 pursuable opportunities.
  • Managed a $150K Google Ads channel and contributed to a broader $10M marketing budget.

Selected artifacts

PhoeniX acquisition integration and Synopsys Photonic Solutions relaunch · OptoDesigner / OptSim / OptoCompiler workflow messaging · 5G and data-center solution content · LucidShape feature and version launch materials · Public product and solution pages · Technical learning resources and launch releases

Applied GTM scenarios

How I would structure, operate, and measure the work.

Launch ownership

Tier-1 portfolio relaunch

Built a 90-day launch plan spanning positioning, product architecture, web, analyst and PR outreach, technical education, webinars, sales enablement, partner activation, and event programming.

Modeled 90-day outcome: 1,800 launch-page visits; 320 webinar registrations; 46 MQLs; 12 qualified opportunities; $720K influenced pipeline.

Funnel economics

Audience-to-revenue funnel

Situation

A media business needed a consistent definition of how anonymous reach became qualified demand and revenue.

Operating approach

Modeled outcome

Modeled quarterly funnel: 30,000 visitors -> 900 leads -> 315 MQLs -> 142 SQLs -> 57 SQOs -> 17 wins; $60K ACV; $1.02M bookings; $12.5K CAC; 2.5-month payback.

03Illustrative / modeled

Voice of customer

Positioning informed by buyer evidence

Situation

Strong product capabilities were not translating into a differentiated buyer story.

Operating approach

Combined 18 buyer interviews, 12 win/loss conversations, 250 survey responses, support themes, and usage data; synthesized jobs, objections, triggers, and proof requirements into a messaging refresh.

Modeled outcome

Modeled outcome: +28% message-test CTR; +17% demo conversion; three roadmap priorities tied directly to recurring buyer friction.

04Illustrative / modeled

Customer journey

Behavior-triggered lifecycle redesign

Situation

Generic onboarding treated every trial user alike and failed to reinforce the behaviors most associated with first-bill conversion and retention.

Operating approach

Redesigned acquisition, onboarding, activation, renewal, and reactivation around behavioral triggers across email, SMS, push, in-app, and transactional messaging.

Modeled outcome

Modeled 40K-user outcome: +18% first-bill conversion; -12% 90-day churn; +0.7 month average retention; +11% reactivation.

05Illustrative / modeled

Adoption experiments

Controlled Content Cards rollout

Situation

A high-value privacy feature had low discovery and fewer than 1% of app opens reached its educational content.

Operating approach

Randomized 20,000 eligible users into 10K control and 10K treatment groups; measured exposed-user activation with retention, opt-out, uninstall, and support-contact guardrails.

Modeled outcome

Modeled result: 85% exposure; 9.4% card CTR; activation increased from 8.2% to 13.6% (+66% relative); p<0.05; no material guardrail deterioration.

06Illustrative / modeled

Leadership system

Ten-person marketing operating model

Situation

A distributed team needed clearer ownership, faster decisions, and more consistent launch quality.

Operating approach

Organized two product marketers, two lifecycle marketers, two content leads, demand generation, operations, design, and analytics around quarterly outcomes, weekly reviews, one-on-ones, launch intake, and explicit decision rights.

Modeled outcome

Modeled outcome: on-time delivery improved from 68% to 92%; campaign cycle time fell 30%; agency spend decreased 15%; two team members promoted.

07Illustrative / modeled

Pricing and packaging

Three-tier packaging redesign

Situation

Feature-led plans created buyer confusion, inconsistent discounting, and weak upgrade paths.

Operating approach

Used 120 willingness-to-pay responses, usage segmentation, competitive benchmarks, and sales interviews to define Core, Growth, and Enterprise packages with clearer value metrics and approval rules.

Modeled outcome

Modeled outcome: +14% premium-plan attach; +9% ARPU; -18% discount leakage; +6% trial-to-paid conversion.
